findings.message: validate_entry promises 'https:// or http://127.0.0.1' but tests loopback by string prefix, so http://127.0.0.1.attacker.example/v1 and http://localhost.attacker.example/v1 are accepted as loopback and a plaintext key-bearing chat call would go to a public host; start.py repeats the same prefix test in run_check.
findings.patch_old:
ok_loop = base.startswith("http://127.0.0.1") or base.startswith("http://localhost")
    if not (base.startswith("https://") or base == "http://127.0.0.1"
            or base == "http://localhost" or ok_loop):
        return "base_url must be https:// or http://127.0.0.1"

findings.message: The only refusal probe uses a plainly public host, so nothing would fail if the loopback check were loosened back to a prefix match; pin the near-miss host that made the guard unsound.
findings.patch_old:
bad["base_url"] = "http://evil.example.com/v1"
    assert providers.validate_entry(bad) is not None
findings.patch_new:
bad["base_url"] = "http://evil.example.com/v1"
    assert providers.validate_entry(bad) is not None
    tricky = dict(entry)
    tricky["base_url"] = "http://127.0.0.1.attacker.example/v1"
    assert providers.validate_entry(tricky) is not None
